children: The European Union has told Britain that raising tariffs on Chinese cars and aligning more closely with EU trade policy could help the country avoid barriers under the bloc’s proposed “Made in Europe” rules, the
reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

“A customs union would solve most of the problems of ‘made in Europe,’” an EU official said, according to the report. “And also the question of tariff differences, which leads to fears the Chinese could avoid our tariffs by routing through the UK.”

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said this week that he would push for Britain to be considered a "trusted partner" under the EU’s proposed “Made in Europe” rules, warning that excluding the UK could damage its car industry.

The policy aims to reduce reliance on Chinese components by prioritizing European-made goods. That could affect Britain’s auto industry, which supplies parts to EU production chains and sells vehicles across the bloc.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said this month that the EU would use “every available tool” to reduce what she called an "unsustainable" trade deficit with China.
The UK currently applies a 10% tariff on Chinese cars, while the EU imposes additional duties on Chinese electric vehicles.
